items.a: Teknoppy's office is located on the second floor of Kaithakal Building, Kaithakal Lane, Thykoodam, Vyttila, Kochi, Kerala 682019. We meet clients in person at our office and collaborate with partners across Kerala, India, and the GCC remotely.

items.q: Does Teknoppy work with businesses in the GCC?
items.a: Yes. Alongside Kerala clients, Teknoppy works with businesses in the UAE and Qatar, with experience adapting sites and campaigns for both regions.

items.q: Can I get website design and SEO from the same team?
items.a: Yes. Every website Teknoppy builds includes SEO from the design stage, so page structure, speed, and content are already aligned with search when the site goes live.

devNotes.origin: No About Us copy doc has been supplied. At the client's instruction, these six questions are reused verbatim from existing pages rather than newly written — each item records its `source` page.
devNotes.duplicateContentRisk: Every question and answer here also appears on the page named in its `source`. The project's docs repeatedly require zero cannibalization, so this set should ideally be reworded for About Us, or replaced once an About Us copy doc exists. The visible copy is duplicated deliberately; see the schema note below for how that is handled.
devNotes.schemaDecision: FAQPage schema is deliberately NOT emitted on /about-us/. Marking up the same Q&A entities on two URLs is what Google treats as duplicate FAQ markup, and the source pages (/services/, /contact-us/, /sanal-edison-digital-strategist/) already own that markup. The FAQ renders visibly for readers; the schema stays with the page that owns each question.
devNotes.pending: Supply an About Us copy doc and this page can be rebuilt like the rest — content in JSON, CMS-editable, with its own FAQ and FAQPage schema.
devNotes.teamSection: The Meet the Team section was hardcoded in about-us.astro and showed only the founder. It now reads from `team` in this file, so members are CMS-editable. The founder keeps the featured card; the rest render as a grid beneath it.
teamDataNeeded: Portraits were converted from the PDFs and PNGs in the client's 'team photo' folder: PDF page 1 rasterised at 200dpi with pdftoppm, then resized to a uniform 1000x1333 (3:4) and encoded to WebP with sharp. Each image is padded rather than cropped, using its own sampled background colour, so no one is cut off and every card is the same shape.

Nandana's and Adithya K's portraits came later, as single-page PDFs of a square (approx 1086px) full-body shot. The embedded image was pulled with pdfimages, then cropped to 3:4 and resized to 700x933 to match the framing the rest of the set settled on (head about 19% down the frame, cut at mid-thigh). These two are cropped, not padded, because padding a square source to 3:4 leaves the bare background bars visible on anjali-babu.webp.
